9195.overview:
Japan-only sequel to Target Earth, Leynos 2 puts you in the cockpit of a giant mecha robot as you scroll and shoot your way through a series of 7 individual missions tied loosely together by a generic sci-fi plot.

The game itself plays as a side-scrolling shooter set in different planets as well as outer space (where you can fly anywhere with your jump-jets). You have a variety of upgradeable weaponry which allow you to shoot anywhere on-screen as well as auto-lock individual enemies, and depending on how well you do on each stage you get a specific rating score that allows you to upgrade and customize your mech.

11282.overview:
Jewels of the Oracle is a stationary puzzle game with no real story line or plot. A total of 24 ingenious puzzles must be solved, each independent of the others. Most of them can be played in two difficulty levels (Easy or Hard), and the Oracle provides clues to help along the way.

The graphics for the puzzles are designed in an Egyptian or Mesopotamian style. Music plays in the background to provide atmosphere, but it can be turned off, if it gets repetitive. The basic layout is a hexagon around an Oracle's well. There are three doors on the outside of the hexagon, and the first one is where you begin the game. In each room is a puzzle you have to solve to get a jewel which must be taken back to the Oracle's well.

The puzzles in this game can be compared to those found in The 7th Guest. The Chinese Checkers puzzle in Shivers rivals many of the ones contained in Jewels of the Oracle.

11283.overview:
The original guitar hero with the Elvis attitude and purple hair pompadour, Johnny Bazookatone, has been imprisoned in the year 2050 in Sin Sin Prison by El Diablo, the Lord of the Underworld, who is jealous of his talent and kidnaps other musical legends as well in this 3D side-scrolling platformer. Johnny's guitar Anita has been taken from him and he sets out to escape and vanquish foes on his way to be reunited with Anita.

He can perform moves such as 360-degree spin jumps, and hover jumps among others, while using his bazooka guitar as a weapon. When powered up, it can emit a special sonic blast that fries anything within hearing range. As you make your way through the demonic levels such as Hotel Demonique, Hell's Kitchen, and Mr. Diablo's fiery Penthouse, you can acquire more weapons, power-ups and find secret passages that lead to bonus levels. The game's soundtrack includes the title track contributed by Bon Jovi guitarist Richie Sambora and Tico Torres.

25570.overview:
This game is the third game in the series of parody shooters produced by Konami and was released only in Japan. The gameplay is stylistically very similar to the Gradius series, but the graphics and music are intentionally absurd. The game, as its name would suggest (translated: "Chatting Parodius Live"), contains a large amount of Japanese voice samples shouted out in a style similar to that of a game show host.

Unlike the previous titles, this game was not created originally as an Arcade game. Instead, it was originally released on the Japanese Super Famicom and this port is an upgraded version of that one, featuring not only improved graphics and sound from the Super Famicom game, but some altered levels and bosses, including a cheat to replace "Tokimeki People's Dance" with an enhanced version, "Days Of The Dream's Memories". Also added were several "Omake" stages and an unlockable Dracula-kun and Kid Dracula as a playable character. In a two-player game, both players can now choose to play simultaneously instead of just alternately in the Super Famicom game.

This game was also released on the Sony PlayStation with little differences compared to this version.

31381.overview:
Following Murder Club, this is another detective story about the fearless private investigator J.B. Harold. This time, an unknown woman in a red dress was murdered in Chicago. A female detective who began investigating the murder was killed as well, and this time the killer made it look like a suicide. J.B. Harold arrives at Chicago and has now to work together with the local police and to solve the mystery.

J.B. Harold: Blue Chicago Blues is an interactive movie. Most of the player's time is spent watching movie footage (with real actors and scenery). At certain points, the movie freezes, and the player is presented with a screen with two or more choices. Each choice advances the clock, so it is necessary to plan well in order not to run out of time and to successfully solve the case.

33043.overview:
Victory Goal '96, the direct sequel to Victory Goal (not to be mistaken for International Victory Goal, which unlike the game in question was distributed for all regions), is the game that set the bases further development of Sega Worldwide Soccer 97 and the sequels.

From the previous games of the series this soccer game just kept the title, because the game engine, music, video scenes and almost everything else, all had the same ingredients that in the West could be seen for first time with the later Worldwide Soccer 97. Also, just as its prequel, this game includes all the teams of the Japanese J.League (of which it had an official license), but on the other hand, it does not include any international teams. The game features commentary tracks by two of Japan's most famous commentators.

33044.overview:
Victory Goal '97 can be considered Sega Worldwide Soccer 97 but with 17 of the teams of the Japanese Professional Football League. Just like the previous Victory Goal games it does not include any international teams, but instead the updated club teams and player names for the 1997 season.

The first in the series not developed by Team Aquila but this time adapted by SIMS, it became the last of the series dedicated exclusively to the Japanese league, and also the last of SEGA games to carry "Victory Goal". Further releases would use the title "Worldwide Soccer", also in Japan.

129165.overview:
Based on the 1995 Rugby World Cup in South Africa and officially licenced by player of the tournament Jonah Lomu, this game plays as more of an arcade style of gameplay rather than a sports simulation. Players can compete in the full World Cup, a round-robin league, or a knock-out cup.

The 32 included teams range from the All Blacks of New Zealand and Springboks of South Africa to minnows such as Namibia and Hong Kong, neither of which qualified for the final stages.

140883.overview:
Mechanical Violator Hakaider: Last Judgement is a light-gun rail shooter with light adventure elements based on the 1995 tokusatsu film Mechanical Violator Hakaider. Set 10 years after the events of the film, the player controls the titular anti-hero android Hakaider as he returns to Jesus Town in order to defeat Professor Gil and recover the arm that he lost in a battle against Waruda.

Each mission consists of one or more first-person shooting gallery-style segments against either waves of enemies or a boss character, in which the player must shoot down targets and projectiles without taking too much damage. The player has several different weapons to choose from, which have different effectiveness and ammo limits. Certain segments also take the form of a simplified first-person adventure, where the player can explore environments and talk to characters, and there are occasional choices for the player to make which may affect the following action sequence.

140887.overview: J.League Go Go Goal! is a soccer game licensed by the Japanese J.League organization and featuring all 17 clubs and full stats for the 1997 season. It includes standard league and exhibition modes and supports up to four simultaneous players. A notable feature of the game is the ability to create custom player formations, and the option to switch between multiple different play strategies on the fly during a match.

140893.overview: This is the Japanese release of the game that in the US is known as Winning Eleven, although it was never actually released in the US for the Saturn. That might be because the Saturn version really wasn't that good of a version.

140894.overview:
Joshikousei no Houkago... Pukunpa is a falling-block puzzle game featuring a cast of cute anime girls who each represent a different school club.

The game plays very similarly to the popular Puyo Puyo series, with colored blobs falling in pairs which must be rotated and arranged by the player. Matching three or more blobs of the same color will cause them to vanish, allowing any stacked above them to fall down and potentially trigger a chain that will send garbage blocks to the opponent. The unique feature here is that some blobs actually contain two different colors; these pieces cannot be cleared on their own, but when a neighboring piece is cleared the double piece expands, releasing the two colored blobs from inside, and allowing for further chain attack potential. If the pieces stack all the way to the top of the well, then that player loses the round.

The game includes two game modes: a versus mode against the computer or a second player, and an endless mode for one or two players. The game also includes an alternate "Funny Mode" which replaces the anime-style girls with crudely-drawn fantasy characters.

140895.overview: Jun Classic C.C. & Rope Club is a continuation of the T&E SOFT New 3D Golf Simulation series. It is played at the Jun Classic Country Club and the Rope Club in Tochigi Prefecture. Unlike most other games in this series, this one offers two golf courses each of which have three different routes of varying difficulty. The game itself is visually similar to other T&E SOFT golf games released around the same time as it runs on what is largely the same engine. Compared to the fixed viewpoint camera of the predecessors, this game features a cinematic camera, along with optional free roaming "golf cart" mode that can be activated from the menu.

140896.overview:
Jung Rhythm is a rhythm action game, whose gameplay is most closely reminiscent of PaRappa the Rapper or Space Channel 5. The player takes the role of Vanilla Essence, a young girl who dreams of being a star, and the story follows her quest from eating breakfast through to a duet with her favourite superstar, the puzzlingly named Mr. Chorking!

The gameplay itself takes the form of call-and-response dance and song duets with various characters, where the other character will sing a line and you’re asked to repeat it. Lyrics appear in a shaded box at the top of the screen, while input prompts appear in the first of a pair of bars along the bottom of the screen as they sing, and the player then repeats it on the second bar. Ad-libbed inputs are also permitted, and there are specific ad-lib segments.

Vanilla Essence’s performance is then graded in five categories and given an overall score. A score above 70 is a passing grade, and allows continuing to the next story segment. Between story segments there is a short full-motion video cutscene connecting the dots.

The game additionally includes a practice mode, as well as a 2-player battle mode, where two players can compare their skills.

157051.overview: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurou! is a football (soccer) management simulation game and the first game in Sega's long-running management sim series. The player takes the role of the owner of a new Japanese football club and must build it from the ground up into a competitive team, with the ultimate goal of the club being admitted to the top league in the country, the prestigious J.League. With only a limited amount of funds available per year, the player must hire staff and scout players, manage sponsorships and publicity, schedule matches and training, and even chose the team's hometown and uniform colors.

157052.overview: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurou! 2 is a football (soccer) management simulation game and the sequel to the first game in Sega's long-running series. The player takes the part of the owner of an upcoming club that is just about to join the prestigious J.League soccer league. As in the previous game, the player manages staff hiring and player scouting, sponsorships and publicity, match and training scheduling, and of course choose the team's hometown and uniforms. New in this entry are the ability to create up to three custom players for the team, additional options for post-match publicity and commentary, and a completely revamped in-game match display system that lets the player watch each match in a much more realistic style.

157053.overview: Japan Super Bass Classic '96 is a bass fishing game endorsed by pro bass fisher Katsutaka Imae. The player is tasked with winning various tournaments on order to win professional titles; winnings can be used to buy and upgrade equipment, with the player's rod, reel, line and lure all being customizable. The game also includes a practice mode to try out equipment before participating in a tournament.

157054.overview:
Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu '95 Kaimakuban is a baseball simulation game. It is an updated version of Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu '95, and also the first in the Powerful Pro Yakyuu series to appear on the Sega Saturn. It features a full NPB license and thus all teams and players from the Japanese Pacific and Central leagues, with rosters up-to-date as of the end of the 1995 pre-season.

In addition to the updated roster, this version features a new set of 12 Scenario mode challenges based on recent games in the 1995 season. The Camp mode, which allows the player to practice the various actions of the game such as batting and pitching, also returns after being absent from the prior release. Also new in this iteration are various assist options to make pitching and batting easier.

157055.overview:
Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu S is a baseball simulation game and part of the long-running Powerful Pro Yakyuu series. It is the second and final game in the series to appear on the Saturn. It features a full NPB license and thus all teams and players from the Japanese Pacific and Central leagues, with rosters up-to-date as of the end of the 1997 pre-season.

New in this entry are the addition of Success mode and League mode, which were both introduced in Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu 3. Success mode is an in-depth training and story mode where the player creates a new recruit and has three years to make it to the starting lineup; Success mode players can be saved with passwords compatible with several other titles in the franchise, allowing a player to be moved between games. League mode is a tournament mode for up to six players/teams. Other returning modes include the Battle (Exhibition) mode, Pennant mode, and Practice mode. There is also a team editor called Arrange mode.

157056.overview: Jikuu Tantei DD is a detective noir adventure game with a futuristic setting. The game is one big cinematic drama which plays as an interactive movie (think Cyberia). The story takes place aboard a zeppelin ship Lorelei. In 2238 human race got the freedom to use the ability to travel back in time, which eventually led to the emergence of crime. You are a Raizou Narukami, a detective who runs an agency that specializes in space-time crimes. Womanizer at first glance, you are very skilled at what you do, namely in power of observation, reasoning and deduction. You are known as DD (short for Dracula Detective) because your are a direct descendant of legendary Dracula. Due to your genes, you also exert some superhuman powers and abilities.

157057.overview:
Jissen Pachinko Hisshōhō! Twin is a pachinko simulation game in Sammy's long-running series of gambling sims. This particular release features faithful recreations of two contemporary real-life pachinko machines made by Sammy:

• CR Gao Gao Kids 4, a dinosaur-themed machine
• CR Kudamonobatake, a fruit-themed machine

The game includes two play modes. The "Real Battle Simulation" mode lets the player set up custom pachinko parlors and must play the machines as they are laid out, starting with a certain amount of money and attempting to increase their winnings. This mode includes detailed tracking of the player's progress and performance. The "Complete Strategy" mode lets the player view detailed information about either machine and play it freely to practice without any money or time restrictions.

157058.overview:
Jissen Pachi-Slot Hisshōhō! 3 is a pachi-slot (Japanese slot machine) simulation game and part of Sammy's long-running series of gambling sims. It features a faithful recreation of five different real-life slot machines from various manufacturers: Aladdin Master by Sammy, Divers XX by Yamasa, Flipper 3 by Universal, Play Girl Queen 2 by Olympia, and Any 7 A by Takasago.

The main game mode is the "Real Battle" mode, in which the player selects one of five characters who each have different income and hours they are able to play, and must conquer a series of gambling halls by successfully earning enough winnings within a certain time limit. There is also the "Strategy" mode which lets the player select any configuration of any of the five featured machines, and practice without any time or money limits. Both modes include detailed progression and stat tracking.

157059.overview:
Jissen! Pachi-Slot Hisshōhō! 4 is a pachi-slot (Japanese slot machine) simulation game and part of Sammy's long-running series of gambling sims. It features a faithful recreation of three different real-life slot machines from two manufacturers: Cranky Condor by Universal, 50's by Sammy, and Aladdin Master X by Sammy.

The main game mode is the "Trial" mode, in which the player enters a custom gambling hall and must earn winnings on each machine inside it. There is also the "Simulation" mode which lets the player select any configuration of any of the three featured machines, and practice without any time or money limits. Both modes include detailed progression and stat tracking.

175164.overview:
Jantei: Battle Cos-Player is a 4-way riichi mahjong game featuring a science-fiction story and a combination of live-action and animated opponents. Set in a futuristic city where the greatest treasures are the costumes of a previous era, the player and their partner Yuko Saionji challenge a series of opponents to mahjong matches in order to collect as many costumes as possible and become the "Jantei", or Mahjong Emperor. Defeating opponents will award their costume, which Yuko can wear and show off in animated or live-action videos depending on which type of costume it is.

In addition to the main story mode, there is also a free battle mode. There is also a "making-of" disc included in the package, which contains a photo gallery and cast interview videos.

175165.overview: Jissen Mahjong is a 4-player riichi mahjong game that offers both 2D and full-3D visuals of the mahjong table. The game includes three modes: Challenge Mode tasks the player with defeating various opponents to increase their rank; while Free Battle Mode and Party Mode let the player choose any three of the 10 available opponents and play a regular match with various options. There are also a wide range of configuration options for adjusting the game rules.

175176.overview:
Jissen! Pachi-Slot Hisshōhō! Iron Hook is a pachi-slot (Japanese slot machine) simulation game and part of Sammy's long-running series of gambling sims. It features a faithful recreation of the Iron Hook slot machine made by Sammy, a pirate-themed machine which was brand new at the time of release. There are two modes: Simulation Mode lets the player choose a particular machine setup and freely play to practice, including detailed progression and stat tracking; Game Mode gives the player a set of pre-configured situations each with a strict time limit and must clear the requirements of each in order.

The game was not sold in stores, but rather was only available as a prize either from certain pachinko halls, or from contests held by publisher Sammy. It comes in an oversize package made to look like an old book with a treasure map inside, matching the pirate theme of the game. Additionally, players could enter a further contest to win pirate-themed prizes like a hand hook or a bottle of rum.

175184.overview: Jungle Park: Saturn Jima (Japanese for Saturn Island) is a point and click adventure game that invites the player to explore the titular park. More a walking simulator than a traditional adventure game, it has few goals and instead lets the player discover the park and its surroundings at their own pace.

182920.overview:
It was Team Aquila's first creation as a sub-department of Sega CS1, and the first in the Victory Goal series. Being released in 1995, it also stands as one of the first 3D football games, though the players are represented as 2D sprites.
Victory Goal was announced alongside the Saturn in early 1994, under the working title of Virtua Soccer. However, it is only assumed Virtua Soccer became Victory Goal - in this early incarnation, only simple demo footage was shown (as was the case for Clockwork Knight, Daytona USA and Panzer Dragoon - only Virtua Fighter was partially playable), with no specific details on the team listings.
Contrary to popular belief, Victory Goal was a Japanese exclusive, featuring teams from the Japanese J. League. Its engine would be adapted and J. League teams replaced with international teams in Sega International Victory Goal. Victory Goal is hence sometimes referred to as J. League Victory Goal to make the distinction.

199022.overview:
Judgement Force is a prototype version of Fighting Force. It was supposed to be released on November 26, 1996, on Sega Saturn, but became unreleased because it was redesigned into Fighting Force. It wasn't released until September 16, 1997. In the original development, the game was originally going to be part of the Streets of Rage game series.

There were differences in Judgement Force, in comparison to what eventually became Fighting Force.

• Alana was not originally in the game.
• The fourth playable character was named Dr. Vulcan.
• Some of the stages were different.
• Mace's age is different. She is 24 in Judgement Force, but 21 in Fighting Force.
• Hawk wears different clothing.
• Smasher and Mace's appearances are also different.
• The loading screen is different.
• Hawk's age is different. In Fighting Force, Hawk's age is 26, but in the prototype Judgement Force, his age is 29.
• Smasher's age is 29 in Fighting Force, but in Judgement Force, his age is 32.
